summary: Top TJR clips (1M–3.9M views) consistently open within 2 seconds on a sharp contrast or ironic juxtaposition — 'ordinary world' (graduation, DoorDash, same-age peers) smashed against TJR's reality (Koenigsegg, cash stacks, luxury cars) — and resolve that tension fast. Lifestyle and mindset clips dominate; trading mechanics rarely appear in the top tier. Clips under 20 seconds dramatically outperform longer ones, with the sweet spot at 7–18s. On-screen text does the heavy lifting: a single declarative statement or ironic label planted in the first 2 seconds (e.g. 'same age btw.', 'The last day on GTA 5') earns the watch. Captions are stripped to one line or one word — the visual IS the caption.
moments_to_pick: TJR delivering a one-liner money or mindset quote in 1–2 crisp sentences — especially anything about silence, not explaining yourself, or skipping the conventional path
TJR reacting with genuine surprise, disbelief, or loud celebration to a big number, an unexpected trade win, or a ridiculous purchase — face fully visible and expressive
TJR physically with a car, exotic item, or large sum of cash — especially if a specific dollar figure is said aloud or visible on screen
A moment where TJR's lifestyle implicitly contrasts with a 'normal' person his age (mentioning peers, college, jobs, or social media critics)
TJR saying something self-aware or funny about his own wealth, reputation, or haters — quotable, clean, no anger
A milestone reaction moment (trade hit, subscriber count, purchase unlocked) with visible emotion — joy or disbelief only, never frustration at people
hook_examples: TJR said this and nobody could argue. 👀
He skipped the degree for THIS.
TJR just dropped a number nobody expected. 😳
title_formula: Lead with a concrete fact or action featuring TJR + one emotional reaction word or emoji. Keep under 60 characters. Formula: 'TJR [specific action or purchase] and [brief punchline or reaction]'. Examples of the pattern (write original): 'TJR paid cash for something most people finance their whole l
caption_formula: One punchy line only — either the exact quotable line from the clip OR a contrast statement framing TJR vs. the conventional path. No paragraph. One optional emoji at the end of the line. Line break, then hashtags on the next line. Example structure: 'He doesn't explain himself. He just wins. 💸\n\n#
avoid: Clips over 25 seconds — views collapse sharply; the 37s 'DoorDash millionaire' clip gets 452K vs 3.9M for sub-10s clips, confirming the pattern
ALL CAPS subtitles — every million-view clip uses sentence case; it reads cleaner against TJR's face-cam framing
Captions longer than one sentence — the top 7 posts use one line or one word maximum; paragraphs signal low-effort reposts to the algorithm
Trading jargon (SPY, NQ, ES, calls, puts, full-porting) in titles or captions unless the clip is purely a reaction moment with no explanation needed
Clips that could read as mocking TJR, showing him losing his temper, or making him look incompetent — campaign rule, and also algorithmically penalised as negative content
Gambling or casino references per campaign rules
experiment: Try a 'split-label' hook: in the first 2 seconds show TWO stacked text labels side by side — 'Their life at 23:' on one half, 'TJR at 23:' on the other, each with a one-word or one-emoji answer below it — then cut hard to TJR's face filling the frame with no hook text. This mirrors the contrast mech
